label: Early copy steps (2nd-3rd output) of long sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, never during the original tokens or at <DEL>. It is concentrated on the first copy-fed inputs: recall_idx 1 (the step right after <DEL>, 66% of mass) and recall_idx 2 (29%), with a little at recall_idx 3, and only when many outputs remain (to_go >= 4, i.e. longer sequences). Rate and mass rise with L: L=9 holds 49% of mass and L<=4 almost none. It never fires on the first occurrence of a token. The predicate (early copy step with >=4 outputs left) gets ~93% of mass but only ~47% precision. Magnitude depends strongly on the identity of the input token: top activations are i or d input right after <DEL>, while many letters (e.g. k, p, q, f) mostly do not fire. Restricting to a high-lift token set (i,d,w,o,m,0,l,a,z,r) raises precision to 0.83 but cuts mass recall to 0.65. So the position gating is clean, but which tokens fire is graded and not fully captured.
